title: Whole Milk 3.25% Milkfat, with Added Vitamin D

content.title: About
content.content: Whole milk with 3.25 % milkfat is fortified with vitamin D (5630). It comes from cows raised on farms that follow quality standards and is pasteurized to ensure safety.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vitamin D in milk helps the body absorb calcium and supports bone health.
Whole milk retains a natural taste and creamy texture thanks to its higher fat content.
Pasteurization kills harmful bacteria while preserving most nutrients.
Milk provides all nine essential amino acids needed by humans.
In many countries milk is sold in 1 L, 0.5 L, and 0.25 L containers.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium is essential for building and maintaining strong bones and teeth, as well as for normal muscle function.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D enhances calcium absorption in the gut and supports the immune system.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Milk protein (casein and whey) supplies all essential amino acids for growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Provides vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is important for red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Provides energy
items.content: Lactose, the natural milk sugar, serves as a quick source of energy.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People lacking sufficient lactase may experience bloating, diarrhea, and discomfort after consuming milk.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergic reactions can include skin rashes, swelling, and in severe cases, anaphylaxis.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: The higher fat makes whole milk more calorie‑dense; those watching weight should moderate portions.

items.title: Spoilage risk
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth and off‑flavors.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Milk can be enjoyed as a beverage, added to cereals, smoothies, sauces, baked goods, and coffee. For children, warm it to a comfortable temperature.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store milk in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. After opening, consume within 5‑7 days. Do not leave milk at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
